title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit

reading.body:
The failure here is not a model malfunction but a misuse of a general-purpose text-generation tool in a context that demands independent, unbiased expert judgment. The expert witness directed ChatGPT to reach a predetermined conclusion, framing the prompt around proving zero fault rather than analyzing the evidence. The output of that process was then submitted as expert testimony in litigation over a deadly industrial explosion, a setting where courts rely on the integrity of the analysis, not just the surface form of a report.

The problem became visible only because litigation discovery exposed the prompts. Without that procedural mechanism, the AI-assisted origin of the report would not have been known to opposing parties or the court. There was no disclosed check at the point of submission, and the report carried the authority of a named human expert regardless of how it was produced.

It is not established that 3M knew how the report was written, that any court has ruled the report inadmissible, or that the expert witness has been found to have committed any legal violation. The lawsuits are allegations, not verdicts, and no findings of liability against any party have been reported.

reports.title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit

summary:
An expert witness hired by 3M to defend the company in a lawsuit used ChatGPT to write portions of his expert report in a case involving a deadly Houston explosion. The witness asked the AI tool to create a report that would show how 3M was zero percent at fault for the incident at Watson Grinding. The prompts he used became public during the legal process, exposing how artificial intelligence was used to generate testimony in this high-stakes case.

The 2020 explosion at the Watson Grinding manufacturing facility in Houston killed three people and destroyed approximately 200 homes. The incident was caused by a degraded rubber welding hose that leaked flammable gas, according to safety investigators. Multiple lawsuits, including a $61 million case, allege that 3M failed to properly maintain the facility's gas detection system. This case demonstrates how AI has entered courtrooms through expert witness testimonies, and that the specific prompts used to create such reports can be discovered and revealed during litigation.
